code_label: Quantum finance application to interest-rate derivatives
text_span: Pricing interest-rate financial derivatives is a major problem in finance
rationale: States the central application domain and problem addressed.

code_label: HJM model as forward-rate framework
text_span: A successful approach to model the latter is the celebrated Heath-Jarrow-Morton (HJM) framework
rationale: Identifies the main financial model used in the paper.

code_label: Trade-off between factors and computation
text_span: there is a trade-off between the number of noisy factors considered and the computational time to perform a numerical simulation
rationale: Highlights the computational bottleneck motivating the work.

code_label: qPCA used to reduce noisy factors
text_span: we employ the quantum principal component analysis to reduce the number of noisy factors required to accurately simulate the time evolution
rationale: Summarizes the main methodological strategy.

code_label: Experimental estimation on IBMQX2
text_span: The principal components are experimentally estimated with the 5-qubit IBMQX2 quantum computer
rationale: States the hardware platform and experimental implementation.

code_label: First quantum computing experiment in option pricing
text_span: This is, to our knowledge, both the first quantum computing experiment in financial option pricing
rationale: Claims novelty of the experiment.

code_label: First step toward general quantum HJM simulation
text_span: This manuscript is a first step towards the design of a general quantum algorithm to fully simulate on quantum computers the Heath-Jarrow-Morton model
rationale: Frames the work as preliminary toward a broader algorithm.

code_label: Practical finance applications expected soon
text_span: It shows indeed that practical applications of quantum computers in finance will be achievable in the near future.
rationale: Expresses an outlook claim about near-term applicability.

code_label: Risk-neutral pricing requires accurate interest-rate dynamics
text_span: it is crucial to model accurately the time-evolution of interest rates.
rationale: Motivates the need for accurate stochastic modeling.

code_label: Short-rate and forward-rate modeling distinction
text_span: Several stochastic dynamics have been proposed in the literature to model either the instantaneous interest rate r(t)
rationale: Introduces the two modeling targets discussed in the paper.

code_label: Short-rate models have calibration and correlation limits
text_span: these models suffer from the strong requirements which arise from the necessity to calibrate to market data and to capture, at the same time, correlation and covariance structures
rationale: States a limitation of simpler short-rate models.

code_label: HJM directly models forward rates
text_span: the celebrated Heath-Jarrow-Morton (HJM) framework, which directly models the time evolution of forward rates.
rationale: Explains why HJM is relevant for the problem.

code_label: Quantum computing promises more computational power
text_span: Quantum computing (QC) has emerged in the last years as one of the most exciting applications of quantum technologies
rationale: Provides the broader quantum-computing motivation.

code_label: Quantum speedup examples cited
text_span: Multiple algorithms with provable quantum speed up with respect to their best classical counterparts have been proposed
rationale: Supports the general case for quantum advantage.

code_label: Small noisy chips limit digital simulation
text_span: State-of-the-art technology, however, only provides us with small noisy quantum chips, which limits the applicability of digital quantum simulations to toy models.
rationale: States a hardware limitation relevant to the experiment.

code_label: Historical cross-correlation matrices used
text_span: The volatility factors are estimated from 2 × 2 and 3 × 3 cross-correlation matrices between different time-maturing forward rates based on historical data
rationale: Describes the data source and matrix sizes used.

code_label: Bond price as discount factor
text_span: P(t, T) is also known as the curve of discount factors
rationale: Defines a key financial quantity used in the derivation.

code_label: HJM drift determined by volatility terms

code_label: Markovianity via time-to-maturity volatilities
text_span: One possibility that ensures Markovianity is to assume that the volatility factors only depend on the time to maturity
rationale: Describes a modeling choice to make the dynamics tractable.

code_label: PCA identifies dominant curve movements
text_span: Using PCA we can obtain the most relevant eigenvectors and their associated eigenvalues.
rationale: States the dimensionality-reduction step used to extract factors.

code_label: Two or three factors often explain most evolution
text_span: most of the evolution of the curve can be explained by considering 2 or 3 of such factors.
rationale: Reports an empirical observation about factor sufficiency.

code_label: Principal components interpreted as shifts and twists
text_span: whenever the entries of the first principal component are all similar, then the dominant movement of the curve will be a parallel shift.
rationale: Provides an analytical interpretation of the first component.

code_label: Covariance matrix from historical forward-rate changes
text_span: we build the covariance matrix between the changes in the forward rates for different time-maturities
rationale: Describes how the input matrix for PCA is constructed.

text_span: The number of entangling gates performed for this algorithm is at least 18, so the total estimated error δ in the coeﬃcients, assuming the 8% error per gate observed in the previous section, is over 100%

code_label: Current processor exhausted by gate fidelity and connectivity
text_span: we have exhausted the computational power provided by the current quantum processor in terms of gate ﬁdelities, connectivity, and number of qubits.
rationale: Summarizes the hardware constraints encountered.

code_label: Lower-level programming could improve volume
text_span: if a lower level programming were available, the optimization of the quantum algorithm adapted to the chip constraints would allow us for dramatically increasing the algorithm volume.
rationale: Suggests a possible route for improvement.

code_label: Work is a first step toward full HJM simulation
text_span: this manuscript is a ﬁrst step towards the design of a general quantum algorithm to fully simulate on quantum computers the HJM model
rationale: Restates the preliminary nature of the contribution.

code_label: Practical finance applications achievable in NISQ era
text_span: shows that practical applications of quantum computers in ﬁnance will be achievable even in the NISQ technology era.
rationale: Concludes with an optimistic forward-looking claim.
